extracted.intended_audience: health care providers, health insurers/issuers, covered entities, legal counsel, state agencies, and stakeholders subject to or commenting on HHS Section 1557 nondiscrimination requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards from the HHS Section 1557 final rule preamble concerning nondiscrimination, accessibility, benefit design, utilization management, and related statutory/regulatory definitions and enforcement principles. Useful for entities implementing or evaluating compliance with the rule and related civil-rights requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental alteration (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined in ADA Title III Technical Assistance Manual as “a modification that is so significant that it alters the essential nature of the goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations offered.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess whether a proposed modification is required; if it is a fundamental alteration, the modification need not be provided. See also Title III Manual for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undue burden (definition and factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined in ADA Title III Technical Assistance Manual as a “significant difficulty or expense.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an action constitutes an undue burden can be determined based on factors including: the nature and cost of the action; the overall financial resources of the site involved; geographical separateness; the overall financial resources of the parent entity; and the type of operation of the parent entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 ICT accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act imposes accessibility requirements for information and communication technology that Federal departments and agencies develop, procure, maintain, or use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to Federal agencies' ICT; referenced resources include 36 CFR part 1194, appendix A and Section508.gov. VPATs are recognized tools for documenting ICT accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) reference
rubrics_metrics.description: VPAT (Section508.gov) referenced as a voluntary template/resource for documenting product accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VPATs can be used by vendors and procuring entities to communicate conformance with accessibility standards for ICT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior authorization (Medicare definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare defines “prior authorization” as “the process through which a request for provisional affirmation of coverage is submitted to CMS or its contractors for review before the service is provided to the beneficiary and before the claim is submitted for processing.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to delineate when pre-service reviews occur; see CMS FAQs for operational details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step therapy (Medicare Advantage definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare defines “step therapy” for the Medicare Advantage Program as a “utilization management policy for coverage of drugs that begins medication for a medical condition with the most preferred or cost effective drug therapy and progresses to other drug therapies if medically necessary.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes a common UM policy; relevant when assessing whether utilization management imposes discriminatory burdens or improper barriers to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durational or quantity limits (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Durational or quantity limits place limits on the frequency or number of benefits to be provided, such as limiting therapy visits to once per week or limiting prescription drug coverage to a 30-day supply of a medication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are types of benefit design limitations that may implicate nondiscrimination or medical necessity considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinically-based non-discriminatory EHB benefit design
rubrics_metrics.description: 45 CFR 156.125(a) states “[a] non-discriminatory benefit design that provides [EHB] is one that is clinically-based.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the CMS standard for non-discriminatory essential health benefits (EHB) benefit design; note enforcement of EHB nondiscrimination is by CMS and is distinct from Section 1557 enforcement by OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of presumptively discriminatory benefit designs (CMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS provided examples of presumptively discriminatory benefit designs applicable to non-grandfathered health insurance coverage in individual and small group markets: (1) limitation on hearing aid coverage based on age; (2) autism spectrum disorder coverage limitations based on age; (3) age limits for infertility treatment coverage when treatment is clinically effective for the age group; (4) limitation on foot care coverage based on diagnosis (whether diabetes or another underlying medical condition); and (5) access to prescription drugs for chronic health conditions (adverse tiering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate benefit design features likely to be discriminatory under CMS' EHB nondiscrimination regulations; enforcement and regulatory reach are distinct from OCR's Section 1557 authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term limited duration insurance (definition and duration limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term limited duration insurance is defined in Federal regulations as health insurance coverage issued under a contract that is effective for less than 12 months, and, taking into account renewals or extensions, has a duration of no longer than 36 months in total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition affects applicability of certain consumer protections and market reform requirements; see 45 CFR 144.103 and related Tri-Department definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered entities must comply with certain ADA accessibility requirements (45 CFR 92.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: 45 CFR 92.203 (section 1557) requires covered entities to comply with certain accessibility requirements in the ADA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1557's accessibility obligations can incorporate ADA principles; the preamble notes parallel regulatory citations in other Departments (Labor, Treasury).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology: gender transition and gender affirmation (usage guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble uses the terms “gender transition” and “gender affirmation” interchangeably in discussing the range of care that transgender individuals may seek; within the regulation, the term gender affirmation encompasses gender transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification is intended to ensure the regulatory text's use of “gender transition” is not read as narrower than “gender affirmation.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1557 vs ADA/Section 504 integration requirements (scope clarification)
rubrics_metrics.description: While the final rule periodically references the ADA and section 504, the requirements under this rule are under section 1557, a separate legal authority; accordingly, the integration requirements under this section 1557 rule do not limit or impact the interpretation of integration requirements under the ADA and section 504.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rule's requirements as distinct legal obligations rather than substitutes for ADA/Section 504 interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Olmstead/integration principles (public entities and services)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOJ materials and cases emphasize that public entities cannot avoid obligations under the ADA/Olmstead by characterizing as a “new service” services they currently offer only in institutional settings; states may violate Title II when they refuse to provide an existing benefit that would enable community-integrated living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to evaluations of whether service location or program changes unlawfully segregate or risk institutionalization of persons with disabilities; case law identifies ‘risk of institutionalization’ and declines in health/safety/welfare as relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctive relief principle (preventing future violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. v. W.T. Grant Co. explains that the purpose of an injunction is to prevent future violations and that such relief is appropriate where there is a “cognizable danger of recurrent violation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in assessing remedies and enforcement actions where prospective relief is sought to prevent ongoing or future nondiscriminatory violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of “statutory objective” (45 CFR 91.12(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 45 CFR 91.12(b) defines “Statutory objective” to mean “any purpose of a program or activity expressly stated in any Federal statute, State statute, or local statute or ordinance adopted by an elected, general purpose legislative body.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant for interpreting obligations and objectives of programs and activities when assessing compliance with nondiscrimination or other statutory duties.
